stories.headline: Uttar Pradesh elections: Samajwadi Party to release election manifesto on November 26
stories.title: Uttar Pradesh elections: Samajwadi Party to release election manifesto on November 26
stories.summary: It will include separate documents for women, youth and a manifesto on law and order, highlighting party’s commitment on these issues apart from focus on social justice and PDA plank
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Samajwadi Party (SP) will release its election manifesto for upcoming 2027 Assembly polls titled “Jan-Man Manifesto,” on November 26, 2026, coinciding with Constitution Day, a date of adoption of the Constitution of India in 1949.

The party president Akhilesh Yadav has announced that the party plans to release the proposed document, called the “Jan-Man Manifesto,” which will highlight outreach to backward classes, Dalits and minority communities.

“The manifesto will focus upon socially and economically marginalized section of the society, that includes women, backward classes, Scheduled Castes (SCs), Minorities and other neglected sections of the society.

We will also include separate documents for women, youth and a manifesto on law and order, it will include our commitment to various groups of people,” told Alok Ranjan, a former U.P. Chief Secretary, who closely worked with the party on policy issues.
After the release of this main manifesto, the party in coming weeks, will release region specific manifestos or district centric manifestos.

On asked about the manifesto release coinciding with the Constitution Day, Nasser Salim, the SP spokesperson said, “On Constitution Day, we reaffirm our faith in the Republic and in the sovereign will of the people.
This manifesto is not merely a political document but a public covenant inspired by the ideals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.
It reflects our commitment to the constitutional empowerment of PDA and every citizen of India,”.
“Samajwadi Party firmly believes in the sanctity of the Indian Constitution which defines India as a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic.
The SP has always stood for the fundamental rights and duties as enshrined in the constitution,” said Ram Pratap Singh, the SP spokesperson.

stories.headline: Why Teaching Post Vacancies Notified Separately For Males & Females? Supreme Court Asks Delhi Govt On Transgender Candidate's Plea
stories.title: Why Teaching Post Vacancies Notified Separately For Males & Females? Supreme Court Asks Delhi Govt On Transgender Candidate's Plea
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has questioned the rationale for notifying teaching vacancies separately for male and female candidates, asking the Delhi Government to explain the legal basis for such gender-based bifurcation and how transgender persons would be accommodated in public employment.

A bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran raised the questions while issuing notice on petitions filed by Jane Kaushik and Praveen Singh, concerning the exclusion of transgender persons from vacancy notifications issued by the Delhi Subordinate Services Selection Board (DSSSB).
The Court asked why the recruitment notification for public appointments continues to be gender-binary, that is, only available for the male and female categories, respectively.
It has passed an order asking the NCT of Delhi what the constitutional or statutory basis is for notifying vacancies based on gender.

It may be recalled that the present petition pertains to a transgender woman, Jane Kaushik, who challenged the Delhi Directorate of Education and the Delhi Subordinate Services Selection Board (DSSSB) notifications for teaching posts as they allowed only binary persons to apply.
This was her second petition before the Supreme Court.
In her original petition, she alleged denial of teaching opportunity and discrimination based on her gender identity, which was recognised by the Court, and she was awarded compensation.
The bench had constituted a committee headed by Justice Asha Menon to undertake policy reforms.
She approached the Delhi High Court on the lack of separate vacancies for transgender persons in teaching jobs and relaxation of minimum requirements of employment by the NCT of Delhi.
However, the High Court disposed of her writ petition, directing her to approach the committee.

Against this, she approached the Supreme Court again, which noted that the High Court committed an error and directed that she be allowed to register herself at the DSSSB's online Academic Registration System(OARS) portal as a transgender person.
However, subsequently, the issue continued to arise since the recruitment notification remained gender binary.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Directs Centre To Publicise Scheme For Interim Compensation To Road Accident Victims
stories.title: Supreme Court Directs Centre To Publicise Scheme For Interim Compensation To Road Accident Victims
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has directed the Union Government to give wide publicity to the Compensation to Victims (Interim Relief) Scheme, 2026, framed under Section 164A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, to ensure that road accident victims are aware of their right to seek interim compensation.

A bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice KV Viswanathan also asked the Centre to clarify whether the scheme covers accidents involving uninsured vehicles, after the amicus curiae Senior Advocate Gaurav Agarwal and an applicant appearing in person pointed out that the scheme appeared to be confined to cases involving insured vehicles.
The Court directed the Union to ensure that the scheme is published in the Official Gazette at the earliest and to inform it by the next hearing how it proposes to make the scheme operational.

The directions were passed on October 16 while hearing contempt petitions alleging non-compliance with earlier orders concerning the implementation of statutory provisions and the publication of road accident data.
The Court noted that Section 164A of the Motor Vehicles Act empowers the Central Government to frame schemes for providing interim relief to claimants seeking compensation.
In an earlier order dated April 28, 2025, the Court had directed the Centre to frame a scheme under Section 164A as expeditiously as possible and, in any event, within four months.
The Court had observed that although the provision came into force on April 1, 2022, it had remained unimplemented for three years.

During the October 16 hearing, Additional Solicitor General Vikramjit Banerjee informed the bench that the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways had framed the Compensation to Victims (Interim Relief) Scheme, 2026.
The bench examined Clause 6 of the scheme, which prescribes the procedure for claiming interim compensation.

Under the procedure, a victim or the legal heirs of a deceased person can apply for interim compensation through a designated electronic portal, along with details of the compensation claim filed or pending before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal.
The application is to be transmitted electronically to the Department of Financial Services in the Ministry of Finance and the investigating officer concerned.
The Department of Financial Services is then required to forward it to the insurer of the vehicle involved in the accident.

stories.headline: India-New Zealand FTA comes into effect, removes tariffs on Indian exports
stories.title: India-New Zealand FTA comes into effect, removes tariffs on Indian exports
stories.summary: The agreement is expected to improve the competitiveness of Indian goods, lower import costs in New Zealand and expand export opportunities.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA), which comes into effect on October 20, will eliminate tariffs on Indian exports to New Zealand, providing greater market access to sectors including textiles, leather, pharmaceuticals and agricultural products, a senior Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) official said on Monday.

Speaking to ANI in Hyderabad, Sampath Kumar, Additional Director General of Foreign Trade, said the agreement would remove existing import duties of up to 10 per cent on several Indian products entering the New Zealand market.
“From tomorrow onwards, the India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement is going to be implemented.
So, under this India-New Zealand free trade agreement, the unique feature is that 100% of tariff lines are going to become zero from tomorrow onwards,” he said.
Highlighting the benefits for labour-intensive industries, Kumar said, “Till now, the maximum tariff on the textile and clothing sector and leather and footwear is up to 10%.
From tomorrow onwards, it is going to become zero.”
He added that tariffs of up to 5 per cent on pharmaceuticals, agricultural and marine products, plastics, chemicals and electrical goods would also be eliminated.

The removal of duties is expected to improve the competitiveness of Indian products in New Zealand by reducing their import costs and providing exporters greater opportunities to expand their presence in the market.
Kumar also expressed confidence that the agreement would strengthen India’s trade position with New Zealand.
“With this free trade agreement, the trade surplus is going to be further increased...
The ties between India and New Zealand are going to be enhanced,” he said.

According to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, bilateral merchandise trade between India and New Zealand reached USD 1.3 billion in 2024-25, registering a 49 per cent increase over the previous financial year.
